label: Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria)
summary: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) bloom in warm, still, nutrient-rich lakes and ponds, mostly in summer and early autumn. Some make toxins that attack the liver, nerves and skin, and looks won't tell you which. Boiling, chlorine and home filters don't make the water safe. Animals, dogs especially, can die within hours.
signs: Water that looks like pea soup or spilled paint, or has scum, foam, mats or paint-like streaks on top, usually green or blue-green, sometimes red or brown
Shallow, warm, slow-moving or still water rich in nutrients, such as ponds and the edges of lakes
An earthy or musty smell, and dead fish, birds or other animals along the shore
Black, brown or green mats growing on the bottom or washed up on the shore
Most blooms come in summer and early autumn, but they can last all year and even grow under snow and ice, and the toxins can persist in the water long after a bloom has ended
do: Treat every bloom as toxic: looking at it won't tell you
Use another source for drinking, cooking, washing food and bathing, and for pets and livestock: stored water or a source with no bloom, treated for germs as usual
Mix infant formula only with water from a safe source
If you touch bloom water, rinse your skin with clean water as soon as you can
Keep dogs and livestock out of it and give them clean water. If a dog goes in, rinse it with clean water straight away, before it can lick its coat
If you have no other water for washing clothes or dishes, wear rubber gloves
dont: Don't boil it: boiling doesn't remove the toxins and can leave more in the water
Don't rely on chlorine or bleach: normal doses don't reliably remove the toxins, and chlorine can burst the cells and release more

Don't count on sunlight bottles or UV pens: they are made to kill germs, and sunlight disinfection doesn't change the water's chemistry. The UV doses that broke toxins down in Health Canada's review were far above germ-killing doses
Don't count on a home filter or treatment system: most small ones can't remove the toxins, and Health Canada says none is certified to remove bloom cells from untreated water supplies
Don't swim, wade or bathe in it, and keep children out: they swallow more water
Don't eat fish organs from bloom water or fish that look sick. BC's health service says to eat no fish or shellfish from bloom water at all
ppe: Rubber or nitrile gloves when you have to handle bloom water or gear wet with it
firstAid: Skin or eyes: rinse with clean water right away, even if nothing hurts
Swallowed: watch for stomach pain, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, muscle weakness, fever or dizziness. Numbness, trouble speaking or trouble breathing is serious and needs medical help
Liver toxins can take days to cause symptoms, so anyone who drank bloom water and then feels ill needs medical help
Dogs: rinse the coat with clean water at once, before it licks it. Animals can die within hours, usually because breathing fails; a dog acting strangely or in distress needs a vet now
